title: Stride-increment time asymmetry fails an exploratory Parkinson gait transfer test
abstract: We tested whether the magnitude of a third-moment stride-increment asymmetry adds information beyond conventional gait summaries and demographics. Source-only standardized logistic models fitted to31 gaitndd participants were frozen for153 gaitpdb participants. Stride-increment irreversibility did not improve frozen Parkinson/control prediction from gaitndd to gaitpdb: Brier 0.364568 versus 0.369608, delta +0.005040, joint95% interval [-0.013068,+0.034851]. Target AUC was 0.4947 versus 0.4829. Both models transferred poorly. This is a model-specific negative result in selected case-control datasets, not equivalence, a diagnostic recommendation, or evidence that time asymmetry cannot carry physiological information.
